chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever strikes a slave with a penalty (hadd) from the penalties, without a penalty having been obligated upon the slave by himself, there is no expiation for the striker except his emancipation.
ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a master who punishes a slave unjustly?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the specific expiation (kaffarah) for a master who imposes an arbitrary or excessive corporal punishment on a slave, mandating manumission as the penalty. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the protection of the slave's rights against arbitrary authority, distinguishing between lawful discipline and unjustified infliction of pain. It reflects the broader Islamic ethical principle that freedom is the ultimate compensation for the deprivation of dignity through unjust physical punishment.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The one who whips an owned (slave), a Penalty (Hadd) from the Penalties, without a Penalty (Hadd) having been Obligated upon himself, there would not be an expiation except for his emancipation (libration)’.
